q1_longest_experiments: The arXiv Bundle v10 task consumed 10 of 16 minutes (62.5%). Root cause: the gate dependency on Exp 1269 (arXiv critical fixes) has not been cleared across seven consecutive milestones (.99 through .107). Each milestone relaunches the bundle task, which spends ~10 min discovering the gate is still blocked before emitting a terminal artifact. The correct fix is an activation-time gate preflight that emits the GATE_BLOCKED terminal artifact in <1 s without spinning up the full experiment.
q2_gpu_utilization: Both RTX 3090s are idle at 4 MB / 0% utilization. No GPU-bearing experiments were scheduled in this closeout-only milestone. DualGPURunner was not used. The 16-min wall time was entirely CPU and conductor overhead. GPUs have been idle at closeout for at least the past seven milestones (verified by gpu_monitor.py output: 0% utilization on both cards).
q3_zombie_processes: No zombie GPU processes observed. Both GPUs show 4 MB allocated but 0% utilization, which is consistent with the driver baseline rather than a leaked process. The gpu_monitor.py suggestions (free memory, use DualGPURunner) are advisory for future GPU-bearing milestones, not indicators of active leaks in this closeout slice.
q4_parallelization: All five experiments ran sequentially. The arXiv bundle gate and three SOTA GGUF doomed-rerun blocks are structurally sequential (each must discover it is blocked before the next launches). True parallelization is only applicable to GPU-bearing research experiments in non-closeout milestones. For this closeout slice, the correct optimization is not parallelism but activation-time gate/doomed-rerun checks that skip blocked tasks in <1 s rather than running them for 2-10 min each.
q5_preflight_bottleneck: Preflight tests are not a bottleneck in this slice. The conductor log for adjacent milestones shows test suites completing in 5-26 seconds. The 16-min wall time is dominated by gate-blocked tasks, not test suite execution.
q6_doc_reconciliation: Doc reconciliation registered 0 min for the in-process docs task (it matched the parent's gate-blocked outcome instantly). This is not a bottleneck. The concern from prior retros — that docs reconciliation is deferred and accumulates — does not apply to this slice.
q7_tooling_improvements: Same three improvements have been recommended for seven consecutive milestones without mechanical enforcement: (1) activation-time gate/DOOMED_RERUN checks emitting immediate terminal blocked artifacts; (2) retirement of Exp 1269 SOTA GGUF cache gate after N consecutive blocks; (3) DualGPU scheduling for GPU-bearing research milestones. The meta-finding is that the retro feedback loop is broken: recommendations are generated but not mechanically enforced by the conductor.
